newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea warns people to prepare for rain.
newsitem.headline: North Korea warns people to prepare for rain.

text.p: Drought-stricken North Korea on Tuesday forecast rainfall in the coming days and warned its hard-pressed people to take precautions to avoid weather-related damage.

Korea Central Broadcast said in a weather report that rainfall of 50 to 100 mm (two to five inches) was expected in the Pyongan, Hwanghae, Kangwondo, Hamgyongnamdo and Chagondo regions by Wednesday, Japan's Radiopress news agency reported.
"In some parts the rainfall may amount to 200 mm (eight inches)," Radiopress quoted the weather report as saying.
Radiopress said the report warned the public to take measures to prevent weather-related damage.
North Korea, already battered by two years of devastating floods, has now been hit by the worst heat wave in 92 years, wiping out crops and driving the Stalinist state closer to mass starvation.
North Korea has had almost no rain since July and about 70 percent of the country's expected maize harvest has been lost, International Red Cross officials said.
